answer: Like a market stall that must pay a saffron merchant's deposit before trading, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake: a walnut-hard bond that is slashed if the agent misbehaves. A Sybil attacker must fund a separate stake per fake identity, so forging a thousand agents costs a thousand bonds, while honest agents earn their deposit back - the same way a sonnet's strict form makes cheap imitation expensive to fake at scale.
